Use case: stylized-concept.
Create one complete Freelancer (2003) spacecraft concept sheet: a NEW REGULAR BOUNTY HUNTER FREIGHTER. The design task is to REINVENT THE LIBERTY FREIGHTER in the BH design language. Start with freighter architecture and design an integrated useful ship.

REFERENCE ROLES, in exact order:
1. Native LI FREIGHTER: PRIMARY architectural authority. Study the elongated, sectional, enclosed cargo ship; distinct forebody, long substantial cargo middle, side mechanisms, changing cross-sections, and separate tapering stern. Develop these relationships in a new body.
2. Original LI freighter sketch: reinforces its dimensional cargo hull, bold stepped shell sections, fan-shaped side mechanisms and structural forebody-to-stern rhythm. Adapt and redesign, do not simply recolour it. Its rectangular cockpit is obsolete for this task.
3. Native BH GLAZING AND FRAME ONLY: the ONLY immutable component. This is a source-geometry reference intentionally excluding the old lower nose. Preserve the original THREE glass panes and their narrow metal framing: one central shield-shaped pane wrapping onto the crown and one rounded side pane on each side, with original boundaries, spacing and curvature. Small top equipment pad in the reference is incidental and need not remain. The crop perimeter is not a mandatory body shape.
4. BH fighter/elite/heavy family: STYLE vocabulary, not an assembly to stretch. Flat swept blades, forward-reaching wing ends, stepped angular supports, purposeful recessed joint regions, slab-to-wedge transitions, cool grey and muted blue-green materials. These traits may change position and proportion. Neither the original fighter body, deep round chin, blunt nose pod, huge upright sail nor the stacked engine layout is compulsory.
5. Regular BW freighter: SECONDARY cargo mass/compact mechanisms reference only.

CRITICAL UPDATED RULE:
Only the glazed cockpit and its immediate FRAME are fixed. EVERYTHING beyond that frame may be redesigned: nose, solid area below and behind the glass, foredeck, collar, belly, engine supports, fins, wings and cargo body. Make the cockpit a SMALL INSERT seated into the NEW angular forebody, not an entire intact BH fighter head bolted to a box. Its native glazing is roughly 2.45 units wide, 1.93 high and 2 long on a player freighter roughly 25-30 units long: short in profile and modest relative to cargo mass. Retain pane shape/scale/orientation, without dragging along the original long curved chin or shell. The new body may extend forward and sideways beyond the glazing, while keeping pilot visibility clear. No new panes or crossbars.

DESIGN QUALITY:
The named architecture below must govern silhouette, cross sections and functional joins. Large connected volumes, a real closed cargo hold, distinct mechanism housings, short purposeful folding wing surfaces, a believable stern. Freighter mass must be in the hull. Explore architectural shape, not the same fighter with a differently sized container. Avoid an egg-shaped cockpit pod, tall humanoid face/chin, giant dorsal fin immediately above the glazing, or a sail added merely as a BH logo.
Maintain left/right structural symmetry. Wings may fold at visible grounded joints with unobstructed exterior sweep; leave room for a bounded two-leaf cargo hatch and its opening. Show flight configuration with hatch CLOSED. Actual new kinematics will be solved in the model; no unverified fold arrows. Equipment pads are small, no guns.
Medium-scale native Freelancer detail: deep panel fields, recessed grilles, stepped shoulders and a few large functional joints. No dense greeble blankets, modeled rivets, exposed pipes, cable bundles, open frameworks/cages, spikes or cathedral ornament.
Regular maintained BH colours: cool light grey panels, darker muted blue-green structural surfaces, dark engine mouths, dark teal native glazing, restrained warning markings. Slight use wear, no pirate patchwork, skulls, red rust or derelict destruction.

PRESENTATION:
Landscape 3:2 sheet, neutral pale-grey studio background, crisp industrial concept illustration with clear shadows and medium surface detail. Upper row: two LARGE views of the WHOLE ship, FRONT 3/4 and REAR 3/4, all appendages inside margins. Lower row: SIDE, true overhead TOP, straight REAR. All five depict exactly the same architecture, engine count, fin positions, wing roots and cockpit placement. True TOP shows vertical fins edge-on; do not replace it with a rotated side view. No isolated tail, scenery, people or explanatory paragraphs. Preserve room around all outlines.

ARCHITECTURE 06 — LONG SECTIONAL FREIGHTER WITH RECESSED SIDE MECHANISMS.
Most directly reinterpret the Liberty freighter. Long narrow hexagonal cargo body, low angular forebody extending ahead of and below the SMALL native glazing insert. The forebody widens into a substantial forward shell band; the cargo middle has broad recessed side fields; an aft band contracts to a narrow solid stern with ONE central round engine. This is not a uniform rectangular box.
Turn the Liberty side fan motif into a partially buried semicircular mechanical housing with three broad angular panels radiating forward into a low movable side blade. The semicircle is a functional side housing, not an exposed wheel. Keep total wing span modest. Use one low swept dorsal blade on the AFT cargo band, well behind the hatch, rather than a tall fin over the cockpit; underside is a closed clipped keel without a hanging BH chin. Long profile with clear slender forebody / cargo / slender stern rhythm. Body dominates; canopy is small and nearly flush into the raised forward deck.

Title exactly: "BH FREIGHTER / BHF06". Labels: "FRONT 3/4", "REAR 3/4", "SIDE", "TOP", "REAR".
